title: Helix Parallelism: Rethinking Sharding Strategies for Interactive Multi-Million-Token LLM Decoding
technique: hybrid KV-parallel attention + TP/EP FFN on the same GPUs with batch-wise communication overlap (HOP-B)

optimized_metrics.evidence: we characterize the full Pareto frontier between throughput per gpu (tokens/sec/gpu) vs. interactivity (tokens/sec/user)
real-time autoregressive decoding under tight Token-to-Token Latency (TTL) constraints
For any given TTL constraint, we report the configuration that maximizes system throughput, forming a unified Pareto curve.
batch scalability, the maximum number of concurrent user requests that can be sustained under a fixed TTL budget

headline_claim.text: Helix reduces TTL by up to 1.5x at fixed batch sizes and supports up to 32x larger batches under the same latency budget for DeepSeek-R1, pushing forward the throughput-latency Pareto

metric_definitions.definition_quote: user interactivity is measured as reciprocal of decoding TTL (token-to-token latency), representing the rate at which new tokens are generated for a single user.
metric_definitions.notes: Per-user rate = 1/TTL, from a simulator, decode-only.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Throughput per GPU is quantified as the total number of tokens generated per second per GPU, reflecting system-wide efficiency.
the maximum number of concurrent user requests that can be sustained under a fixed TTL budget
metric_definitions.notes: Used interchangeably with 32x higher Tokens/s/GPU in §3.2.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: real-time autoregressive decoding under tight Token-to-Token Latency (TTL) constraints
metric_definitions.notes: Per-step decode latency of one token for each user; never formally defined beyond reciprocal of interactivity.

slo_spec: latency budget is a TTL sweep (Pareto), no fixed SLO
load_regime: decode-only simulation sweeping 100,000+ configurations over TP/EP/PP/KVP and batch size at 1M context
tradeoff_acknowledged: Pareto trade-off throughput/GPU vs tokens/s/user: higher batch raises throughput but lowers per-user rate; Helix shifts frontier outward.
extractor_notes: Most explicit tokens/s/user vs tokens/s/GPU Pareto framing in the batch. Interactivity is a decode-only per-step quantity; no queueing, prefill, or percentiles. Cites Medha for vanilla KVP.
load_class_quote: "we opt to leverage an in-house high-fidelity simulator modeling the latest GB200 hardware" (§3, txt line 280); decode-only, "we simulate decode-time" behaviour at 1M context
repass_log: TPS_USER, TOKEN_LAT, THR_TOK, batch_scalability: all design (Pareto objective/TTL constraint statements); no percentile stated, stat_basis unspecified for TPS_USER and TOKEN_LAT
